why: The criterion holds for all four verifier checks. Check 1 tests only what "exports clamp(x, lo, hi), which returns x limited to the range" requires: clamp is exported, the argument order matches the signature, and the outputs are correct for values below, above, inside and on the edges of the range. Check 2 only asks that lo>hi throws a RangeError. Check 3 only asks that each exported function is documented ("its name with its signature or a description"). It names no headings and requires no exact wording. Check 4 only asks that the tests pass with no failures. Everything stricter sits under "Advisory (not part of any PASS or FAIL above)": the exit status 0 requirement, clamp tests existing, a clear RangeError message, the mutation idea, and existing exports behaving as before. No PASS or FAIL condition adds a branch rule, file-scope rule, exact message text or mutation test.
